entities.name: Glutaric acidemia type 1
observations: Glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causes elevated C5DC, urinary glutaric acid, and 3-hydroxyglutaric acid.
Typical infant presentation includes macrocephaly and frontotemporal CSF-space widening; encephalopathic crises may follow febrile illness.
Management includes carnitine supplementation and reduction of lysine and tryptophan intake, with avoidance of catabolism and fasting.

entities.name: Lysine
observations: Dietary lysine restriction is a core component of treatment for glutaric acidemia type 1 because lysine degradation produces glutaryl-CoA.

entities.name: Tryptophan
observations: Tryptophan restriction or reduction accompanies lysine restriction in glutaric acidemia type 1 because tryptophan is also a precursor of glutaryl-CoA.

entities.name: L-carnitine
observations: Carnitine supplementation is used in glutaric acidemia type 1 to replenish low carnitine and facilitate removal of accumulated glutaryl groups.
